body.html: GreenView Boutique Hotel is a 4-star boutique hotel on Wongwiwat Road in the centre of Su-ngai Kolok · The building is 6 storeys with around 57 rooms · What has lifted it to #1 of the hotels in Su-ngai Kolok on TripAdvisor is a standard of cleanliness and decor a notch above the older hotels typical of a border town · Su-ngai Kolok sits on the border with Malaysia's Kelantan state, at the end of the southern railway line and beside a crossing point, so most guests are travellers in transit, traders and people on cross-border business — which makes a clean, central hotel like this genuinely valuable.

The rooms are what guests praise most consistently · They're clean, spacious, with strong air conditioning and comfortable beds · Many have balconies, flat-screen TVs, a safe and good water pressure · The decor feels properly boutique rather than a bare guesthouse room · There's free Wi-Fi throughout, free parking, a 24-hour front desk and an airport-transfer service (for a fee) for those who fly into Narathiwat and continue to Su-ngai Kolok · Downstairs there's a lobby café, a restaurant and bar, and a small garden with a fish pond that the kids like to watch.

"Very clean, spacious rooms with cold air conditioning, friendly and helpful staff, a varied breakfast buffet, and an easy walk to the railway station and market — the best hotel you'll find in Su-ngai Kolok."

The breakfast buffet comes up often too · There's a good variety of savoury and sweet options, handy for fuelling up before you travel on · The overall feel is quiet and homely, and the orchid garden and fish pond out front make it more relaxing than a bare tower block · Location is the clear advantage — it's about 650 metres from Su-ngai Kolok railway station, near the central mosque and the town market, with restaurants and shops within walking distance, and not far from the border crossing for anyone heading over to Rantau Panjang in Kelantan.

Honestly, from real reviews: it isn't flawless on every detail · Some reviews mention small things in certain rooms not working perfectly — the odd Wi-Fi router, a fridge, or an adjustable shower rail — which happens, and staff usually sort it out once you flag it · Another point is that online booking rates can run higher than the walk-in rate at the desk in some periods, and it's priced a little above other hotels in town — but you're paying for the cleaner, higher standard · Staff English is limited, as it generally is across Narathiwat, but they're kind and go out of their way to help.

In short, if you're in Su-ngai Kolok to change trains, cross the border or handle business in this border town and you want somewhere clean, safe and walkable to the station and market, GreenView Boutique Hotel is the most sensible choice in town — and it's ideal for a one- or two-night stop along the way · But if you're expecting resort-grade facilities or lots of in-hotel activities, a border town like this won't deliver that, because the appeal here is the location and the cleanliness, not luxury.

A tip from following the reviews here: compare the online rate against calling or walking in at the desk first, since the on-the-spot price is cheaper in some periods · If you arrive on the southern line into Su-ngai Kolok station, you can walk to the hotel easily without a taxi · If you want a newer, quieter room, ask for a higher floor away from the road when you book · And if you're crossing into Malaysia, check the border opening hours and have your documents ready, since the crossing is close and you can move on quickly.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — GreenView Boutique Hotel Su-ngai Kolok

faq.q: Where is GreenView Boutique Hotel, and what's nearby?
faq.a: GreenView Boutique Hotel is at 84 Wongwiwat Road in central Su-ngai Kolok, Narathiwat Province · It's about 650 metres' walk from Su-ngai Kolok railway station, near the central mosque and town market · It's not far from the border crossing for anyone heading to Rantau Panjang in Kelantan, Malaysia · Narathiwat Airport is about 55 km away.

faq.q: How much does GreenView Boutique Hotel cost, and how do I book?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿1,000/night for a Standard Room · Superior/Twin and King Suite rooms run around ฿1,200–฿1,600 · Prices depend on the period and rate, with some rates including breakfast · Compare on Agoda, Booking and Trip.com first, and try calling or comparing the walk-in rate at the desk, as it's cheaper than online booking in some periods.

faq.q: What are the rooms and breakfast like at GreenView Boutique Hotel?
faq.a: Rooms are clean, spacious, with strong air conditioning and comfortable beds, many with balconies, flat-screen TVs, a safe and good water pressure · Breakfast is a varied buffet, with a lobby café, a restaurant and bar, and an orchid garden with a fish pond · This standard is what makes it #1 in Su-ngai Kolok on TripAdvisor.

faq.q: Who is GreenView Boutique Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers changing trains on the southern line, people crossing the border into Malaysia, and anyone on business in this border town who wants somewhere clean, safe and walkable to the station and market · It's ideal for a one- or two-night stopover · It's less suited to anyone expecting resort-grade facilities or lots of in-hotel activities.

faq.q: Does GreenView Boutique Hotel have parking and an airport transfer?
faq.a: Yes · The hotel has free parking, free Wi-Fi and a 24-hour front desk · There's an airport-transfer service (for a fee) for those who fly into Narathiwat and continue to Su-ngai Kolok · Ask the hotel for the transfer details and price in advance of your trip.

faq.q: What are the reviews like for GreenView Boutique Hotel?
faq.a: It's currently ranked #1 of the hotels in Su-ngai Kolok on TripAdvisor · Guests who have stayed praise the cleanliness, spacious rooms, cold air conditioning, good breakfast and helpful staff · The things to allow for are small details in some rooms that may not all work, prices a little above the neighbours, and a border town that suits a stopover more than a long stay.
